cards.text: It's the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and Jesus's disciples come to Him with a question about the Passover. I respect a crew that plans ahead. I once preheated the oven AFTER the dough was ready, and that dough just sat there STARING at me.

cards.question: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, what do the disciples ask Jesus about the Passover?

answers.text: Where He wants them to prepare it
Who He wants them to invite
How long the feast should last

cards.text: Jesus sends them into the city to a certain man. No name, just a certain man, which is like me telling a baker 'grab the bowl' in a bakery with FORTY bowls.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to say the Teacher will keep the Passover with His disciples at the man's ___.

cards.text: Here's the Teacher's message: 'My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.' So the disciples do just what Jesus directed and get the Passover ready.
When evening comes, Jesus is reclining at the table with the twelve disciples. Then, while they're eating, He says, 'Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.'

cards.question: When Jesus says one of the twelve will betray Him, the disciples are deeply grieved.

cards.text: Then, one after another, they ask Him, 'Surely not I, Lord?' It's like when the smoke alarm goes off in my bakery and every baker slowly turns around to check their OWN tray.

cards.question: Jesus gives the disciples a clue about who will betray Him. What does He say that man has done?

answers.text: Dipped his hand into the bowl with Him
Sat closest to Him at the table
Arrived last to the Passover meal

cards.question: Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man, and He says the Son of Man will go 'just as it is written about Him.' What does that mean?

answers.text: What happens to Him was already in Scripture
His words will all be written down later
His name is kept in the temple records

cards.question: Jesus says woe to the man who betrays Him, and that it would be better for him if he had not been born.

cards.text: Then Judas speaks up, one of the Twelve and the one who would betray Jesus. Same question, one word swapped: 'Surely not I, Rabbi?'

cards.question: Judas asks Jesus, 'Surely not I, Rabbi?' How does Jesus answer him?

answers.text: Go and do what you planned

cards.text: While they're still eating, Jesus takes bread, speaks a blessing and breaks it. Then He gives it to the disciples.

cards.question: Jesus gives the broken bread to the disciples and tells them to take and eat. What does He say the bread is?

cards.text: Then He takes the cup, gives thanks and gives it to them: 'Drink from it, all of you.'

cards.question: Jesus says the cup is His ___ of the covenant, poured out for many for the ___ of sins.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them He won't drink of this fruit of the vine from now on. And He tells them exactly how long that lasts.

cards.question: Jesus says He won't drink of the fruit of the vine from now on. Until when?

answers.text: Until He drinks it anew in His Father's kingdom
Until the next Passover in Jerusalem
Until the Feast of Booths at the temple

cards.text: Then they go out to the Mount of Olives. Friend, I can feel this night getting heavier with every step.

cards.question: Before they go out to the Mount of Olives, Jesus and the disciples sing a hymn.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, 'This very night you will all fall away on account of Me.' ALL of them, and He backs it up with Scripture.

cards.question: Jesus quotes Scripture: when the Shepherd is struck, the sheep of the flock will be ___.
Right after the hard news, Jesus gives the disciples a promise. What does He say He'll do after He has risen?

answers.text: Go ahead of them into Galilee

cards.text: Then Peter, one of the Twelve, speaks up: 'Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will.'

cards.question: Peter says he'll never fall away. What does Jesus say Peter will do this very night, before the rooster crows?

answers.text: Call out to Him three times

cards.text: Peter doubles down: 'Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.' That's me telling my bakers I will NEVER burn a batch, and I said it with smoke coming out of my hat.

cards.question: Peter is the only disciple who says he'll never deny Jesus.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave them for now, out on the Mount of Olives with some big promises hanging in the air. This night's not over, friend, not even close.

findings.problem: The joke makes Jesus's directions the punchline. It compares 'a certain man' to Papa Dorin giving a useless instruction in a bakery with forty bowls, which says Jesus's directions were vague. That pokes fun at Jesus. It also suggests the disciples couldn't tell who the man was. The text never says that, and verse 19 says they did as Jesus directed.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: 'And He tells them exactly how long that lasts' says more than the text does. Jesus only says 'until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father's kingdom.' He gives no exact length of time.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only one that sounds like Scripture ('drinks it anew', 'His Father's kingdom'), and the two wrong answers are everyday calendar dates. A baker can pick it by tone alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. In verse 35, Peter makes a bold promise about the future. In the joke, Papa Dorin breaks his promise while he is making it ('smoke coming out of my hat'). That turns Peter's vow into one that was already false when he said it, which is not what is happening in the verse.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
